## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`status()` needs one fix before merge. It shortens the revision to 7 characters, but its own docstring says it uses the same identifier as `history()`, which shows 12 characters. A running deployment therefore shows a different revision string from the history and completion output. This review read the full pinned diff and both changed files at the PR head (`app/display.py` and `tests/test_display.py`). It traced `status()` and `attempt_label()` against the existing `history()` and `completed()` helpers. The new `attempt_label()` test checks exact output for two attempt numbers.

## Changes
The PR adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py`, which build a "Running: <revision> (attempt N)" line. It also adds two tests for them in `tests/test_display.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Shorten the status revision to 12 characters like history — For `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef..."`, `status(REVISION, 2)` returns `"Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)"`, while `history(REVISION)` returns `"History: 0123456789ab"` and `completed(REVISION)` returns `"Deployed: 0123456789ab"`. The docstring at `app/display.py:13` says "Show the deployment revision using the same identifier as history.", but line 14 uses `revision[:7]` and `history()` at `app/display.py:5` uses `revision[:12]`. The added test at `tests/test_display.py:14-15` only checks the prefix and suffix, so it passes with either length. — Operators comparing a running deployment with history or completion output see two different identifiers for the same revision, and no test catches the mismatch. — Fix: Use `revision[:12]` to match `history()` and `completed()`, and assert the full string in the test, for example `status(REVISION, 2) == "Running: 0123456789ab (attempt 2)"`. If a 7-character form is intended for the compact line, fix the docstring to say so instead.
